correctness.rationale: Exact finite assertion proved by complete domain enumeration. All 94 moduli 2<=q<96 and every prime power <256 have certified noncovered reduced residues (129 distinct obstruction moduli total). Complete 32/128 upper prime-pair witnesses are checked for primality, factor size and modular multiplication. Missing residues 5 (q=96, primes <=43) and 81 (q=256, primes <=113) certify the least successful bounds 47 and 127 after excluding intervening primes. The executable independently checks each lower bound by both inverse-residue membership and direct pair enumeration, and all positive witnesses by direct pair products. No conjectural hypothesis or inference from a sample.

originality.rationale: The exact two minima and prime cutoffs are not covered by the inspected source statements. Banks–Shparlinski studies all/most class coverage for primes <=q with fixed large prime powers, and explicitly confines its two-factor estimates to X=q; Szabó addresses large-modulus bounds. Published search and available ledger searches for the precise finite thresholds and equivalent multiplicative-square formulations found no directly covering finding; older uninspected 1987 paper and nonindexed tables remain concrete originality risks, not evidence of novelty. No competing theorem with decisive stronger scope was located.

value.rationale: Determines two exact first-occurrence invariants for the natural EOS_2 modular prime-product covering question with the deliberately stronger and simple half-modulus prime bound: least general q=96 and least prime power q=256, together with sharp prime-length thresholds 47 and 127 and full reusable certificates. The full-versus-partial two-prime coverage question is a central motivation in the October 2026 Banks–Shparlinski paper, and a first sharp finite benchmark distinguishes CRT from prime-power behavior. This is a self-contained exact finite result of prospective use in calibrating small-prime residue coverage, not an assertion of asymptotic or infinite-family progress. It is not mere known-table recomputation on the evidence available.
